summary: The trace shows a common pattern: pandas unavailable, requiring fallback to openpyxl for Excel operations. This skill captures the openpyxl patterns for reading/writing Excel files, which is reusable across many tasks that involve spreadsheet data.
Enhanced excel-file-operations skill with column-oriented data reading and row-finding patterns that were used successfully in this task but weren't documented in the existing skill.

The trace shows the agent successfully created Excel output files but failed verification because the generated data contained logically incorrect values (massive negative backlog values). The agent only verified file structure (headers, row count) but not data sanity. Adding validation guidance to the existing excel-file-operations skill will help future agents catch calculation errors before submission.

The agent's output passed self-validation but failed the verifier test, likely due to column misalignment when extracting multi-row data from the spreadsheet. Adding extraction verification and multi-row layout handling to the existing excel-file-operations skill will help future agents catch this class of error earlier.

The trace reveals reusable patterns for working day calculations with holidays, cumulative formula construction, and date-based conditional logic in Excel workbooks. These patterns extend the existing excel-file-operations skill with production planning and scheduling capabilities.

The trace shows a production planning task where the agent successfully used the existing excel-file-operations skill but encountered a datetime vs date comparison error that required explicit normalization. The skill already mentions this issue in troubleshooting but lacks a concrete fix pattern. Adding a date normalization code example and a brief production planning workflow will help future agents avoid this error and work more systematically when building capacity-constrained schedules.

The trace shows an agent that successfully used the existing excel-file-operations skill patterns but failed the verifier tests despite claiming success. The key gap is insufficient validation of business logic constraints and over-reliance on self-reported success. Adding explicit multi-scenario validation patterns and stronger verification guidance will help future agents catch errors before declaring completion.

Updated excel-file-operations skill to handle string dates from Excel cells, clarify the values_only=True vs .value access confusion that caused AttributeError, and add guidance on iterative constraint satisfaction for production planning scenarios.
